title: County business turnover diverges sharply by the sector through which residents experience place
source_unit: US county-sector; Census Business Dynamics Statistics 2023 county-sector flows
geography: United States; 3,194 counties and county equivalents in the 2023 county-sector table

denominator.unit: county-sector rows with comparable entry, exit, and net-job rates

observations.method: Descriptive county-sector summary of reported BDS rates; disclosure-marked values were excluded rather than treated as zero.
observations.uncertainty: County-sector aggregates do not identify firms, survival, ownership, wages, service use, or sampling uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: A positive median does not mean most residents experienced better access or work; 1,245 comparable rows had negative net-job rates.

denominator.unit: county-sector rows with comparable entry, exit, and net-job rates

observations.method: Descriptive county-sector summary of reported BDS rates; disclosure-marked values were excluded rather than treated as zero.
observations.uncertainty: Transportation flow is not passenger or worker mobility, and county-sector aggregates do not identify firm-level or household consequences.
observations.counterinterpretation: The near-zero median and 1,387 negative rows show that a county-level growth label can conceal contraction in a mobility-relevant sector.

denominator.unit: county-sector rows with comparable entry, exit, and net-job rates

observations.method: Descriptive county-sector summary of reported BDS rates; disclosure-marked values were excluded rather than treated as zero.
observations.uncertainty: Employer job flow is not provider availability, appointment capacity, care use, quality, or household benefit.
observations.counterinterpretation: Positive median job flow coexists with 1,051 negative rows and does not establish adequate or reachable care.

observations.period: 2023; same-county sector counterexample, Ohio county FIPS 39/089

denominator.unit: selected sectors with at least 100 reported establishments in the county

observations.method: Within-county comparison restricted to four selected sectors with at least 100 reported establishments each.
observations.uncertainty: The transportation rate may reflect a small denominator or large establishment changes; this is not a causal case study.
observations.subgroup: One Ohio county; retail, transportation, health/social assistance, and accommodation/food sectors.
observations.counterinterpretation: The same county can show contraction in retail while transportation, health, and food expand; aggregate county conditions do not identify the experienced service or work system.

related_sources.claim: Census documents the BDS establishment and job-flow program.

boundary: This is a 2023 county-sector aggregate flow layer. It does not identify firms or applications, establish survival or causation, or measure service access, prices, wages, household burden, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. Raw BDS data were retrieved transiently; the committed retrieval hash covers the analyzed suffix.
